On the real surface, with a transaction in database postgres holding an id taken at 0 s and at 3 s after /healthz, the first cold stream got the event committed during the wait 0.29 s and 0.08 s after the holder ended. The proof is still rejected, on cost, at the production size INFRA-514's architect named (at least 5,000,000 events). The fix reads every id of the log from 0 at every process start, because nothing proves a horizon at boot. The implementer's figure of about 0.6 s per million is about 0.75 to 0.84 s per million on this 2-vCPU pod (3.6 to 4.2 s at 5M, psql). Also, GitHub reports the PR conflicting.

failures.evidence: Red test 41ec0a4139de: TestTheRelaysFirstStartDoesNotReadTheWholeEventLog in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/server_test.go. It fills 200,000 published events and opens the first cold stream, then counts events_pkey index tuples read (pg_stat_user_indexes.idx_tup_read). It fails at the head twice: 'the relay's first start read 200008 index tuples of events_pkey on a log of 200000 events, want at most 20000'. It passes when the start's read is bounded to the newest 1,000 ids (a local edit I reverted, used only as the test's control). Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:16432/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestTheRelaysFirstStartDoesNotReadTheWholeEventLog -count=2 -v. Real surface, on a log of 5,000,123 ids (4,995,108 rows, 5,015 rollback gaps, 910 MB) with no transaction held, on a newly started head process: the first cold GET /api/v1/events opened 3.75, 3.75 and 3.98 s after its request (main e82b013b: 0.015 s). On the first resuming stream, which opens at once, an event posted right after waited 3.23 s to arrive. The gap read alone took 4.20, 3.59 and 3.71 s in psql. EXPLAIN: an Index Only Scan of events_pkey over 4,995,108 rows, then a WindowAgg, 4.5 s. The cost is linear in the log, so a log of tens of millions waits tens of seconds after every restart, and every deploy (D2: one replica, recreated) pays it. It holds no lock that blocks writers: only AccessShareLock on events, 0 ungranted locks in 33 to 36 samples while it ran, and 62 to 63 comment POSTs during each start all 201, p50 14 ms, max 147 ms. Inference: an AccessShareLock held for 4 s or more makes a migration that takes AccessExclusiveLock on events wait, and writers then queue behind that migration. Fix direction is the implementer's: bound the first start's read, for example to ids above a recent floor, rather than scanning from id 0.
